claims.text: High-temperature annealing increases the coercive field of magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is annealing an initially as-cast alloy at 1000°C for 1 hour.
Annealing reduces lattice defects and residual stresses.
Modification of stress and defect structure produces a more stable magnetic-domain configuration.
A more stable magnetic-domain configuration increases coercivity.
Annealing will produce a 20% increase in coercive field relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast baseline coercive field is 500 Oe.
The predicted effect should hold at room temperature for magnetic fields up to 10 kOe.
The proposed effect is bounded to annealing temperatures below 1200°C and times below 2 hours.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may depend on alloy composition and annealing conditions.
Failure of the annealed sample to achieve at least a 10% coercive-field increase would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 20% increase, but the falsification rule rejects it only below a 10% increase. An observed increase between 10% and 20% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
